newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares lose 2.16pct, test 1,450pts support.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares lose 2.16pct, test 1,450pts support.

text.p: Greek shares lost 2.16 percent in a broadly-based retreat, adding to last week's cumulative 7.71 percent drop on poor sentiment, brokers said.

"Following a period of rapid improvement in macroeconomic indicators, there is now a stall in the flow of favourable inputs from the macroeconomy with prices adjusting to a rigid core inflation and higher short-term interest rates," said broker Michael Pappas at Hermes Brokerage.
Investors long for a pleasant surprise in macroeconomic indicators, preferrably inflation, he added.
Other brokers said the market was affected by foreign selling, with domestic institutionals attempting some selective buying in blue chips.
In technical terms, the market was seen oversold by brokers, having reached a strong technical support level.

"From a technical point of view, the market has retraced 50 percent from its late May peak to current levels," said Pappas. "This indicates that stocks are becoming oversold after a sell signal was given by a clear head-and-shoulders formation around 1,650 points."
A strong support level at 1,450 will be tested in the near-term, he added.
Shares of OTE telecom continued to trade actively around 6,600 drachmas.
Dealing in OTE also included the trades for the transfer of a total 53.4 million shares of OTE which were recently part-floated.
"Selling pressure on OTE was sparked by the price differential between the book-building price and the market price in the previous weeks," said Pappas.
The stock now suffers from a broader deterioration in market sentiment, though retail and domestic institutional investors are reluctant to adopt a bear tuck, he added.
The Athens general index settled 2.16 percent or 32.45 points lower at 1,467.92 from Friday's 1,500.37, recording an intra-day low at 1,450.39 around mid-session.
The downbeat mood was depicted across the board, with all sub-indices recording severe losses, led by banks, off 2.66 percent, and industrials 2.64 percent.
Turnover reached an astonishing 640.2 billion drachmas on volume of 99.3 million shares due to the transfer of OTE's part-floated shares through the bourse's automated trading system.
Trading in OTE's shares produced turnover of 624.9 billion drachmas.
Decliners beat advancers 164 to 50 with 30 shares unchanged on 244 traded.
OTE telecom OTEq.L Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $12.25-$12.30. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,112-1,142 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,197-1,257 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument were unchanged at 6,600 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 466.40-496.17 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $62.97-$64.66. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 2,705-2,911 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $9.19-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 175-204 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
